title: Every edge of a closed trail lies on a cycle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $c$ be a closed trail in $G$ based at a vertex $u$ — that is, a walk from $u$ to $u$ that traverses no edge more than once — of positive length. Then every edge $e$ appearing in $c$ lies on a cycle of $G$: there is a vertex $v$ and a cycle based at $v$ whose edge set contains $e$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
c is a closed walk from u to u
c is a trail (no repeated edges)
e is an edge of c
replaced:
\emph{If an edge \texttt{e} is in a closed trail of \texttt{G}, then \texttt{e} is
in a cycle of \texttt{G}.}
